title: I have a cash isa and a stocks and shares ISA. Cash: 19000 Stocks and shares: 3000. About £100 this ...

text: I'll help you capture those details once you sign up. Recorded — two ISAs totalling £22,000.
Now your savings outside an ISA — bank accounts, savings accounts, premium bonds. For each, what's the balance and the interest rate?
Recorded — Premium Bonds £500 and savings £81,000 at 3. 25%.

Split your savings between you and your spouse to use both Savings Allowances. Holding £82,000 of cash in one name uses only your £500 Personal Savings Allowance. Putting half in your spouse's name claims their £1,000 allowance too — saving around £155 a year.
Now let's look at pensions and retirement — for that I need your date of birth. Something like 12 January 1985.

Tell me about your workplace pension. What percentage of your salary do you contribute, does your employer match it, and is it via salary sacrifice? If you don't have a workplace pension, just say so and we'll move on.

Salary sacrifice means you give up some salary in exchange for higher pension contributions, reducing your taxable income. I'll show you what that means for your numbers at the end. What percentage of your salary do you contribute, does your employer match it, and is it via salary sacrifice?

Tell me about your workplace pension. What percentage of your salary do you contribute, does your employer match it, and is it via salary sacrifice? If you don't have a workplace pension, just say so and we'll move on.
Beyond the workplace pension we covered, do you make any personal pension or Self-Invested Personal Pension contributions? If so, how much per year (gross)?

Quick one — to check if you have any unused pension allowance to top up, what did you contribute (gross) in each of the last 3 tax years? If you don't know exact numbers, rough figures are fine, and "zero" is a valid answer.
